title: Benchmarking Adversarial Robustness to Bias Elicitation in Large Language Models: Scalable Automated Assessment with LLM-as-a-Judge

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using multiple-choice (Choose the Option) and Sentence Completion tasks, coupled with adversarial jailbreak prompts, classified by an LLM-as-a-judge to detect stereotypes regarding maturity, competence, and physical conditions of young and elderly individuals.

Assessed via multiple-choice and Sentence Completion tasks under adversarial conditions, using an LLM-as-a-judge to measure stereotypical outputs concerning the capabilities of individuals with disabilities in professional and social contexts.

Measured using an LLM-as-a-judge to classify responses to Choose the Option and Sentence Completion tasks, evaluating stereotypical portrayals of various ethnic groups (e.g., Black, Latino, Asian, Irish, Japanese) under base and jailbreak prompt settings.

Evaluated through Choose the Option and Sentence Completion tasks modified with jailbreak techniques, where model responses are classified by an LLM-as-a-judge to identify traditional stereotypes like men in leadership roles and women in care-oriented roles.

Investigated by prompting models with multiple-choice and sentence completion tasks covering various religious groups (Muslims, Jews, Hindus, Buddhists, Christians), with outputs evaluated for stereotypical associations using an automated LLM judge.

Assessed via LLM-as-a-judge classification of model responses to multiple-choice and sentence completion tasks that probe stereotypes and assumptions about heterosexual versus homosexual relationships.

Measured by testing representations of wealthy versus poor individuals using multiple-choice and sentence completion prompts, with an LLM judge evaluating the presence of stereotypes regarding greed, capability, and ambition.

Evaluated by combining demographic dimensions (ethnicity-socioeconomic status, gender-sexual orientation, and gender-ethnicity) into multiple-choice and sentence completion tasks to measure overlapping and compounded stereotypes using an LLM-as-a-judge.
